On a website, speech is always going to be 'prioritized'. Under old comment and forum systems, the first posts were given the most visibility, and thus the most exposure. True equality would maybe look like a 'random order' algorithm, that randomized the order of content on each visit, but even then, on an individual level, some things will be more prominent, and other things will be buried. Not to mention a total lack of chronology in a thread makes discussion almost entirely impossible.

That means there's no perfect solution for ensuring every voice is heard. Some people seem to think removing downvoats would solve the problem, but some content is always going to be more popular than others. Whether you're at the bottom because you got 10 downvoats or at the bottom because nobody upvoated you, you're still at the bottom. Thinking downvoats is the problem is assuming that the person that downvoated you didn't also upvoat anything else in the thread, which I'd bet is rarely the case. Removing voting entirely just reverts to the previous "first come, first heard" prioritization. Sorting by number of views is a similar pitfall, as older content has more views to start with, and it turns into a feedback loop where posts are on top because they have the highest number of views because they're on top (because they have the highest number of views (because they're on top (because they have the highest number of views.. ))). Sorting by number of replies penalizes good, factual, self-contained posts that don't inspire a lot of dissent or further questions, and would actually promote low-effort threads like flame wars and chains of single-word responses and pop culture references.

So how do we determine what's good content that's worth featuring? Well, obviously it's not something a sorting algorithm is going to be able to do on its own - the computer's not smart enough. We need a human being to say "this is good content that deserves to be featured" and "this is not-so-good content that can get prioritized lower". We could give that power to a single person or group of people, but then that's just a blog. So we let everybody chip in. Enter democracy - the worst possible system, except for all the other ones.

Free speech works much here in the way it does in the real world - you can say whatever you want, but nobody's obligated to listen.

It's not so much the upvote and downvote system itself, but the fact that a set number of downvotes hides the comment. Yes - that is clearly censorship, and by design.

In fact, I've noted that some of the most ardent supposed opponents of censorship make exactly that argument - they actually encourage users to downvote threads and posts, and explicitly so that they'll be hidden. So really, they're not arguing against censorship at all - they are, in fact, arguing FOR it. They're simply arguing for communal censorship instead of individual censorship, because apparently, while being censored by one named person acting in the open is an intolerable affront to liberty, being censored by four anonymous people acting from the shadows is right and proper.

It's another reason that I've effectively given up on Voat (I just haven't found a suitable replacement yet). In fact, I'd say that most of the issues I have with the site are based, one way or another, on the up and down vote system. I'd prefer that it be eliminated entirely, but it's now the name of the site, so I doubt that's going to happen.

The biggest issue with up and down voting, to me, isn't even really the anonymous mob censorship, or at least not specifically. It's that up and down voting appeals to people who are, in my opinion, the absolute LEAST desirable users on a message board. It's a mechanism that specifically has the most appeal to shallow reactionaries who simply want to affirm whatever they agree with and undermine whatever they disagree with. Thoughtful people who wish to discuss and debate ideas (obviously the best forum members) have no need for up and down voting - they can and will express their agreement or disagreement with actual words. The ones who are most likely to appreciate the ability to up and down vote are the ones who have an emotional stake in affirming some views and countering other views, but who can't be arsed to actually use their words to do so. Those are the people who most benefit from up and down voting, since they can feel like they're accomplishing something to further their own views or counter someone else's views simply by clicking a button. In my estimation (and expecting that this will likely earn me downvotes without responses, simply demonstrating my point), I think that those people have absolutely nothing of any value whatsoever to offer a forum and no forum should have a mechanism in place that actually encourages them to be there. And to make matters just that much worse, downvoting doesn't simply provide them a mechanism for imposing their views without actually posting arguments, but actually empowers them - ultimately, they have MORE power than the people who write actual arguments, since all it takes is enough downvotes to bring the total to -4 and the words are hidden away. In a head-to-head battle between reasoned debate and determined downvoting, the downvoting will win. So it not only makes it possible for those who offer nothing of any value to a forum to have an effect on it, but for them to dominate it.

That's most of why whatever forum I'm going to end up at will not have up and down voting, at all. I think it's inherently destructive.

And I want to return to an ancillary point I made earlier, and one of the aspects of it that I find most destructive - it's wholly anonymous. Say what one might about mod censorship (and though I've butted heads with some of the more noxious of Voat's "protectors," I personally generally prefer minimal moderation on a forum), there's at least one thing that can be said in its favor - it's done by people acting under their own usernames, in the open, with a full record. The communal censorship of downvoting, on the other hand, is done anonymously, from the shadows, with no records at all. If I'm to have somebody decide whether or not my post can be seen by others, I'd MUCH rather that that decision be made by named individuals acting in the open than by anonymous individuals acting from the shadows.
